note: Second-wave stress fixtures. Fabricated content plus renderings of PUBLIC legal PDFs. No firm data.

quirks: every cell is boxed -- the easy case, and the control against which the borderless fixtures are read
Arabic label column, English label column, Western numerals
degraded: -0.3 deg skew, noise 4, JPEG q82
six columns with narrow gutters -- tests whether cell splitting survives when the inter-column gap approaches the inter-word gap
no ruling lines except one header rule
degraded: 0.4 deg skew, noise 6, JPEG q78

files.structure: 4-column table with EMPTY CELLS in every column
quirks: blank cells on purpose: a reconstructor that assumes full rows will shift contents into the wrong column rather than emit a gap
Arabic-Indic numerals in the case column against Western numerals in the date column
most degraded of the three (JPEG q72) -- tests the table geometry under recognition noise
degraded: -0.6 deg skew, noise 8, JPEG q72
deepest numbering in the corpus -- tests whether the structure detector builds a heading path rather than flattening every level to the same rank
letter and roman sub-levels mixed with numeric ones (.a, .b.i)
every clause appears twice, once per language, so a chunker that cuts on markers must not treat the English restatement as a new clause

files.language_mix: Arabic and English alternating WITHIN single sentences
files.structure: numbered memorandum paragraphs, no article markers
quirks: the hard bidi case: direction switches mid-sentence, several times per line, around parenthesised English glosses
Latin terms embedded in Arabic clauses ('عقود الـ finance lease') -- language detection must return mixed, not pick a winner
quoted English inside Arabic inside brackets: nested direction runs

files.structure: articles plus lettered exhibits, roman appendices, numbered schedules, and bracketed footnote references
quirks: four parallel numbering systems in one document (Article 1.1, Exhibit A.1, Appendix II.1, Schedule S1.1) -- a detector keyed on one of them will mis-rank the others
footnote markers [1][2][3] inline in clause text, with the footnote bodies collected at the end behind a rule
annex headings appear after the operative text, so document order and clause-id order diverge

files.structure: a single 30-row table that spans a page boundary, with a repeated header row on the continuation page
quirks: the table is ONE logical table but TWO page objects. Extractors that work per page report two tables; the header row appears twice; a chunker with keep_tables_whole must decide which of those is true
the continuation page's first row is a repeat of the header, not data
counted as 1 expected table on purpose -- reporting 2 is the failure mode this fixture exists to surface

files.ground_truth_provenance: AUTHORED -- the text was written first and then painted onto the page, so the reference is correct by construction
quirks: clean 300 dpi equivalent, minimal degradation
NO text layer -- must be classified scanned and routed to OCR
the reference has no visual-order, fragmentation or out-of-flow defect, unlike every reference derived from a source text layer. **These are the fixtures whose absolute OCR accuracy is quotable.**
still optimistic against real scans: rendered glyphs, no scanner optics, no photocopy generations, no bleed-through
exercises: OCR accuracy on a clean reference
